clue.text: Collection prior to wedding of Jeanne Lorioz?

definitions.meaning: a store of linen and household goods a bride-to-be puts by, the British equivalent of a hope chest
a French painter whose plump women are always shown from behind, so whimsically an artist of rear ends

explanation.surface: A trousseau gathered before the marriage of a Frenchwoman named Jeanne Lorioz.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase as a drawer (artist) of bottoms; the question mark flags the whimsy. In Britain the first sense is a young woman's store of linen kept for married life.
explanation.definitionFit: British idiom for the household linens and goods saved up by a woman ahead of marriage.

clue.text: Intolerant former kids' TV favourite accepts nothing

indicators.note: the TV favourite takes in, or accepts, the zero within its letters

parts.note: Big Ted, a teddy bear on the British children's programme Play School
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A beloved old children's TV character turns out to be a bigot who accepts nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Ted was one of the toys on Play School, a long-running BBC children's programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bigoted person will not tolerate opinions or people unlike their own.

clue.text: Principle of European red wine bottles

indicators.note: the wine holds the abbreviation inside it, as a bottle holds a drink

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine, an old crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A principle held by a continental red wine producer about bottling.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is a dark red wine from Spain, chiefly used for communion.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tenet is a core belief or doctrine held as true.

clue.text: Where a coat may be hung immediately

definitions.text: Where a coat may be hung
definitions.meaning: literally, hooked over a peg driven into the wall
paying at once, without delay, as in an idiom for prompt payment

explanation.surface: Hanging up a coat straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for prompt payment, and also literally the peg on which a garment hangs.

clue.text: So-called pacifist used wooden club to despatch rook

indicators.note: to despatch is to send away, so the chess piece's letter is sent out of the word

parts.note: in golf a driver is a wooden club, so using one is to have driven, past tense drove
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A self-styled peace-lover killed a rook with a wooden club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So-called' admits the label is figurative: in politics the peaceable side are called doves, as opposed to hawks.
explanation.definitionFit: Political metaphor: someone favouring peace and negotiation over war is labelled after the bird of peace.

clue.text: One transferring property is hard worker with injured groin

parts.note: a donkey is a beast of burden that toils hard

indicators.note: an injured body part is damaged, so these letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A property conveyancer is a hard worker who has hurt his groin.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal term: the party who makes over a right or property to another is called this.

clue.text: At last, income tax raised, which entertains Papa; he has emigrated

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is wanted
the reversed word entertains, or hosts, the letter inside it
in a down entry raising a word turns it upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: P is Papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Income tax finally went up, so Papa left the country for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' takes E from income; 'raised' turns TAX into XAT, and 'which entertains' sets P inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a person who has left their homeland to live abroad is an expatriate.

clue.text: Furious about apparatus in water

indicators.note: the angry word goes about, or around, the equipment

parts.note: furious means irate
a rig is a set of apparatus or equipment

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about some equipment that has ended up in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water' looks like a noun after 'in' but is the verb definition; 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to supply land or crops with water through channels is to irrigate.

clue.text: Bidets out of place in single-room accommodation

indicators.note: letters out of place have been moved about into another order

explanation.surface: A bidet looks incongruous in a one-room flat.
explanation.walkthrough: A bedsit is a British term for a rented single room used for both living and sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: British term for a rented single room that serves as bedroom and sitting room.

clue.text: Some words in case information is blocked by bit of technology I possess

indicators.note: the first pieces are blocked, split open, by the rest going in between

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
is shortened to an apostrophe-s gives S
IT, information technology
I've, short for I have

explanation.surface: A news story is blocked by some gadget I own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocked by' splits the information-plus-is piece in two. 'in case' sounds like a precaution but is grammatical: these are nouns in the possessive case.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar: nouns in the possessive case, like Latin forms showing ownership, are words of this kind.

clue.text: Quiet desire to empty bowels

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
an urge is a desire

explanation.surface: A quiet but pressing need to visit the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical sense: to clear out the bowels with a laxative is to purge.

clue.text: Upper-class idiot was at the front

parts.note: tit is British slang for a fool
led means was ahead, in front

explanation.surface: A posh fool was at the head of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone holding a noble rank such as lord or duchess belongs to the aristocracy.

clue.text: Vanity projects of English resulted in tears

parts.note: got means brought about, produced as a result
rips are tears in cloth

explanation.surface: Pet schemes of the English ended in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' reads as weeping, but it is rips in fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: self-indulgent undertakings done mainly to boost one's own image.

clue.text: Awful upset when pound replaces yen

indicators.note: the money unit in the clue takes the place of the other letter

parts.note: dismay as a verb means to upset or distress
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen
L, from libra, is the abbreviation for pound

explanation.surface: A currency trader is upset when sterling takes the place of Japanese money.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something dismal is dreadful or dreary, very poor in quality.

clue.text: Overdue money in Albania is returned, and is pinched

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the run of letters reads in reverse

parts.note: late means overdue
the lek is Albania's currency
is shortened to apostrophe-s gives S

explanation.surface: Overdue cash in Albania comes back, and gets stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinched' tempts as stolen; here it is thin and drawn in the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pinched, gaunt face is bony and very thin from hunger or illness.

clue.text: Resolute competitor ignoring time limits

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: a contestant is a competitor

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its outer letters

explanation.surface: A determined competitor pays no attention to the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits' takes T and E from time, and 'ignoring' drops them from CONTESTANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: steadfast and unwavering in loyalty or purpose.

clue.text: Getting rid of Tory leader instead of Conservative stalwart

indicators.note: one letter stands in place of the other

parts.note: scrapping means getting rid of

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A party loyalist ditches the Tory leader in favour of a Conservative stalwart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' gives T from Tory; 'instead of' puts it where C was in SCRAPPING.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: strongly built and sturdy, as with a big strong lad.

clue.text: Queen leaves bribe for tennis side

indicators.note: the royal abbreviation leaves, departing from the word

parts.note: a backhander is British slang for a bribe
ER, Elizabeth Regina, abbreviates Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen walks out after a bribe in a tennis match.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis term: the stroke played across the body, and by extension the court side it is played on.

clue.text: Without giving anything in return, take bust of leader

definitions.text: Without giving anything in return, take

indicators.note: bust means broken, so these letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Seize a sculpted head-and-shoulders of the leader, paying nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a statue but is the anagram signal on 'of leader'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to scrounge, accepting food or lodging from others while giving nothing back.

clue.text: Start of female prerogative

parts.note: a prerogative is a right or privilege

explanation.surface: The beginning of a woman's privilege.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' reads as a beginning; it is a sudden jump of alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a start is a sudden shock or scare that makes one jump.

clue.text: Grand expression of contempt over politicians?

definitions.note: the plural noun names party members, matching the plural answer

parts.note: G is slang for grand, a thousand

indicators.note: in an across clue over means turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a sneer is a contemptuous expression

explanation.surface: A large display of scorn aimed at politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of an environmentalist political party, nicknamed after their colour; the query flags the nickname.

clue.text: Ranges of new carpets

indicators.note: new means remade, so these letters are formed afresh

explanation.surface: A shop offers ranges of fresh carpets.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: spectra are the full ranges or bands, as of colours or opinions.

clue.text: Sick criminal possesses impressive climbing tools

indicators.note: the rearranged word holds the other inside it
criminal means bent, so these letters are bent out of shape

parts.note: epic means impressive, grand in scale

explanation.surface: An ill criminal owns some fine mountaineering gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' scrambles the ill word into ICKS, and 'possesses' wraps that around the grand word.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: mountaineers hack footholds in frozen slopes with these pointed axes.

clue.text: Primate spin-dries clothes

indicators.note: as a verb, clothes means covers, so the phrase dresses the answer inside it

explanation.surface: A monkey runs the clothes through a spin-dryer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like laundry but is a verb: the words clothe the lemur's name. The indri is a large Madagascan lemur.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the indri is a large lemur of Madagascar, and lemurs are primates.

clue.text: Brief is not in bed with partner

parts.note: up means out of bed, risen
a date is a partner for an evening out

explanation.surface: A short note says someone is not in bed with their partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' is the verb, to give someone the latest information.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to brief someone is to bring them up to speed with the latest news.

clue.text: Opposed to holy man being deported once more

indicators.note: being deported means sent out, so these letters leave the word

parts.note: against means opposed to
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: Someone is against a holy man being expelled for a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: again means one more time, a repeat.

clue.text: Free love enclosure

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: Free love behind a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: open means unrestricted, available to all, free.

clue.text: Difficult to conceal source of oil supply

indicators.note: the hard word conceals the letter, wrapping around it

parts.note: hard means difficult

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: It is hard to hide where the oil supply comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a hoard is a stockpile or supply kept in reserve.

clue.text: Candidate from Spanish city nearly receiving pesetas

indicators.note: the shortened city takes in the money letters
nearly means not quite, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: Alicante is a city on Spain's Mediterranean coast
P is an abbreviation of peseta, so two give PP

explanation.surface: A job candidate from a Spanish city is almost being paid in old Spanish money.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone applying for a job or place is a candidate for it.

clue.text: Copenhagen dancer has this covert plan

parts.note: the word for a plan of business is concealed in the letters of Copenhagen dancer

explanation.surface: A Danish dancer harbours a secret scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a description of the clue: c-open-h-AGEN-DA-ncer carries a programme of business concealed across its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a secret motive or scheme behind someone's stated purpose.
